The reader now handles vendor_b files in UTF-8 as well as cp1252, which was the next item in your memory notes. All 23 tests pass. It isn't committed yet, and I haven't been able to test it against the real file that fails.

**Where things stood:** `main` was clean. The speed-up and the 2,000-row chunk size were already committed in 79857a8. Next up was the cp1252 fallback for that real vendor_b file that won't decode. We still don't know why it fails, because I don't have the traceback or the file.

**What I changed:**
- **`ingest/reader.py`:** each vendor now has a list of encodings to try in order, and the first one that decodes the whole file is used. vendor_b tries UTF-8 first, skipping a byte-order mark if there is one, then cp1252. UTF-8 has to go first because cp1252 accepts almost any bytes: it would read a UTF-8 file without an error but garble the accented characters. vendor_a stays UTF-8 only. If no encoding works, you get a clear `ValueError` instead of a raw decode error.
- **Tests:** four new cases:
  - a UTF-8 file containing bytes that cp1252 can't decode (the likely cause of the real failure)
  - a UTF-8 file with a byte-order mark, which would otherwise break the first column name
  - a cp1252 fallback that keeps "Café – noir" intact
  - a file that can't be decoded at all
- **`README.md`** wording updated, and a **`CHANGELOG.md`** line added under Unreleased.

One cost: each file is now read twice, once to detect the encoding and once to parse it. It's streamed, so memory use stays flat, but it adds some I/O on very large imports.
